subject: Return an unordered_set of unresolved codepoints
message:
This is fine, though in the future you may end up wanting "unresolved runs" so that if multiple code points in a row are unresolved then the user also knows that a whole run was unresolved and also so the user knows where that run was in context so they could maybe re-shape even more or have more information when doing font resolution. It might also be somewhat helpful in the future to return with those runs the resolved language/script (so that the right fonts might be picked for Han unified code points).

In other words, this is a fine first step, but for a more robust solution in the future you're going to want to return a list of unresolved code point ranges, each annotated with the corresponding script and language.

message:
This can be backed by ICU, but using ICU here seems misleading. The point seems to be to provide and abstract interface to unicode algorithm implementations, so SkUnicode might be better, since that seems be the goal. I suppose this same comment goes for the name of this file.

Rambling note about naming follows:

For historical reasons Skia has both SkFontMgr_fontconfig and SkFontMgr_FontConfigInterface. The FontConfigInterface name has been the source of a lot of confusion over time (especially since the file name was originally even more confusing) when the point of the class was to be a remote abstraction so the user didn't need to know what it was backed by. If you're trying to hide an implementation detail, probably shouldn't put the implementation detail in the name.

Also note std::map which should have been named std::rb_tree and std::unordered_map which should have been named std::hash_table_chained. These have the opposite problem, using too generic a name for an implementation.

Naming things is hard.

subject: Use std::span for SkSpan
message:
I don't understand why this is still in progress since it is obvious that std::span is still quite inferior and we aren't gaining anything from this change (at the API side there is no overhead difference when taking SkSpan and the user passes in a std::span and internally there is no benefit and a lot of awkwardness). At the very least because there is nothing gained then there is no hurry and the bazel toolchains should be updated first if they are an issue, and we can even wait for C++23 to get `begin` and `end` at least.

In fact if what we want is to have std::span and not SkSpan at the public API level then that is fine. I'd be fine with a change that internalized SkSpan and the API is forced to take std::span and then we just let the (implicit) conversion to SkSpan just take place internally. But it doesn't make a lot of sense to convert to std::span internally at the moment because it is so deficient to the point that [Chromium technically bans its use](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/styleguide/c++/c++-features.md#span_banned).

subject: Use std::span for SkSpan
message:
Using `std::to_address` is not "easy" and would almost always be the wrong thing to do anyway (just iterate). Unfortunately std::span doesn't seem to get any love because everyone wants to work on ranges instead.

If there is a real need for an extent param it could be added to SkSpan, or you could just use std::span for those few cases. That's fine.

There is no benefit to any of this change so there should be no detrimental defines or other silly additions to "support" it with older toolchains. Since there is no benefit it must be at least neutral.

This is only accidentally "enforcing" size_t discipline because in C++20 std::span still doesn't have a constructor taking an initializer list (it's supposed to get one with C++26!). Which is also why the ridiculous number of braces. I'm all for converting more or less all the `int` counts in Skia to `size_t` though.

We're not dropping anything that duplicates the STL, since the STL doesn't do what we want. `std::span` has lots of sharp edges (like T needing to be complete).

subject: Use std::span for SkSpan
message:
Actually, the compiler error is correct (and only being allowed as an extension by some implementations) because `std::span` states `ElementType is required to be a complete object type that is not an abstract class type`. So it is not possible to have a `std::span<EnlosingType>` without undefined behavior. Deleting the implicit copy constructor does "work around" this particular implementations UB, but this is still UB with `std::span`. `SkSpan` was written explicitly to allow this. See also https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/106988 .

There may be more of these instances elsewhere that we don't know about.

subject: [pdf] Better structure element kids order
message:
While this prevents strange collisions, it does not actually put the child spans in order. It is possible that the user lists the children in one order and then draws them in the opposite order. Possible other approaches:

1. Scan from last child to first child and ensure each span starts at the minimum seen so far. Then emit kids "in order".

2. The simple approach of emit any kid that "comes before" the next child.

subject: [pdf] Better structure element kids order

However, we also don't want to do a lot of work to figure out the original intent. If that is ever wanted there will need to be some way for the user to explicitly state where they want each draw to end up in the structure tree explicitly.

message:
The idea here is that reporting an SkFontStyle would reflect the SkTypeface state but providing an SkFontStyle to a lookup would allow synthetics if the corresponding bit is set. This is a bit awkward, but any sharing of "reported state" and "request" is always a bit awkward.

Also, as this is synthetics are off by default, which is true for most reported styles, but false for most requests. That being said, only the SkTypeface implementations actually report SkFontStyle and users are generally creating SkFontStyle for requests. So the SkTypefaces being updated would mean making them default allow (unless `SK_WIN_FONTMGR_NO_SIMULATIONS` is set).

subject: Allow synthetic bold and italic in request
message:
The issue here is that on a request it makes sense to have yes/no/maybe, but this is incompatible with the equivalence operator that is currently mostly being used in tests.

This is similar to `SkFontParameters` and `SkFontArguments`. `SkFontArguments` turns out to be quite useful to flexibly make a request (when providing font data) because all the information is needed and it is a specific request. `SkFontParameters` has turned out to be less useful because it is generally not necessary to get all the information all at once. Instead of using `SkFontParameters` there are just individual `getXXX` on `SkTypeface` to get each piece of information.

Applying this to the current issue, it makes some sense to expand SkFontStyle into `SkFontRequest(Arguments)` which is like `SkFontParameters` but for making a request against a collection instead of request against a font file (though the line between these two is getting smaller). This would not have a `operator==`. `SkTypeface::fontStyle` would be removed and replaced with `getWeight`, `getWidth`, `getStyle`, and `getSlant` (and of course `isSyntheticBold` and `isSyntheticOblique`) instead of adding a `SkFontRequest(Parameters)` which would be as unused as `SkFontParameters`. If adding a new thing anyway for the future, the existing SkFontStyle can just be allowed to remain as-is for now while adding the new `SkFontRequest`.

subject: Better font request
message:
As a comment to the future, "character" here is not a great name, it is more legacy and is closer to how OpenType documents the cmap Format 14 table. If fully going with OpenType names here, this "CMapEntry" is a "UVS" (Unicode Variation Sequence) which consists of a "base character" and a "variation selector". However, it is also used for non-UVS (no variation selector) purposes. The naming here is something of a compromise.

From a user (and maybe even implementation) point of view it might make sense to just allow a string of UTF-8 here. However, while putting together this interface it seemed best to make this extremely explicit.

While this isn't being taken by the other shapers yet, it probably should be. Currently we have a few that allow words to wrap and other which do not, but they should all be able to do both (not that we actually need to implement that yet).

This particular proposal is nice in that it is high level and implementable. Unfortunately, it is high level and not very general (difficult to allow the user to just muck with the suggested line endings). The more general version of this is to add yet another callback to the shaper interface so that for any line ending found the user can choose to force extend (or maybe contact) it (both of which may make the line longer or shorter, and not necessarily always which way one would expect). So there would be a CoreText version of that extender (which would look like this) and maybe an ICU version, and a do-nothing version. Then the user could pass one of those or their own function in.

subject: [Fontations] Add palette index bounds check in COLR rendering
[Fontations] Add palette index bounds check in COLR rendering
message:
I think this is a good change, even if Skrifa ends up checking the values in the future (and it isn't clear if Skrifa should be doing that or not). While the current bounds checks mean that this isn't a full security issue it is true that Skia should not be crashing when it is clearly possible to continue.

That being said, it isn't correct to return or continue early from these methods. The FreeType COLRv1 implementation was written around the idea of being able to skip drawing subtrees and reporting that back up the stack. However, the Fontations COLRv1 implementation isn't written that way and does not currently have a way of reporting that back up the stack (and making it do so would be a much larger change). As a result, it makes more sense here for Fontations to simply "draw the wrong color" rather than "skip drawing".

Also, you should add yourself to the `AUTHORS` file.

One way to keep that is to move `dest_stops.push_back` down with `dest_colors.push_back`. However, skipping a stop completely is a bit awkward and may lead to other issues.

It would be better to use some random color here, like `SkColors::kMagenta`. This ensures that all the stops are represented and have an associated color. The use of an out of bounds palette index is already incorrect behavior, so any color will do.

subject: Expose SkFontMgr_custom_directory.cpp for skia_renderengine_deps
message:
You must not use any SkFontMgr. Which directories do you think you are going to scan with `SkFontMgr_custom_directory`? You do not even have read access to the randomly named font directories for updated fonts. How are you going to do lookup? You must not request fonts by name as you will have no idea what their names actually are, and this is always buggy to begin with. How would that ever handle variable fonts? You do in fact need to serialize the font data and all its parameters (variation position, color palette, collection index, etc) and deserialize them. You will also need some way to keep track of typeface identity to prevent sending all this information for every draw call.

You may use a SkFontScanner, but you will need to be sure to use the correct one (FreeType or Fontations) based on the system flags.

subject: Expose SkFontMgr_custom_directory.cpp for skia_renderengine_deps
message:
I fail to understand how you would even be specifying fonts or loading them at all with a directory font loader? How would you even do font matching? At what level are you even trying to do this? If you're doing it at the view level then just depend on Minikin and you don't need any of this. Otherwise the application is just drawing using some (parameterized) font data and a bunch of positioned glyphs, in which case you don't have any information about where to look up the font data so you need to send it.

Any yank measurements would be uninformative if not measuring the need to serialize and deserialize the fonts (and parameters) as would be necessary. What is the point in the measurement if not measuring what would need to be done?

subject: [pdf] Map marked content in non-page streams
message: After taking a look at the test output (like the output of `imagefilters_xfermodes`) on this patch set, it became obvious that beyond the "simple" issue of not emitting all the references reserved this change also relies on the idea that SkPDFDevices are used once. But sometimes the current content of the device is moved into a form xobject content stream with the content then referenced from the page and the device continues to be used. https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1177977/3 does get around this (by adding one more layer of indirection, the solution to all our problems) but there are still a few more things that need to be cleaned up.

subject: [pdf] Map marked content in non-page streams
message:
As pointed out by running `imagefilters_xfermodes` this change suffers from the fact that SkPDFDevices can be "reused". (See uses of `this->makeFormXObjectFromDevice` which dump the current content into a form xobject so that it can be re-used as an element of subsequent content.) This means that it isn't generally possible to know the actual content stream reference up front like is tried here. For example this may have started out looking like Page content, but it got pulled out into a form xobject randomly, so when making the marks we don't know which content stream reference they will end up in.

As a result, the content stream reference will need to be made when actually emitting the stream (as is currently done). However, the structural parent tree stream entry and key can be made with the marks (as is done in this patch set) so it can be updated later with a ref to the content stream (when it actually exists). This means the marks don't need to each hold on to the content stream ref (which they cannot know anyway as they are being created as they don't know which content stream ref they will end up in) but they will need to hold onto the struct parents key so that later they can find the reference to the content stream. One will need to be careful to reset the structure parent key then the device is reset (but keep the current active structure element).

Also one will need to be careful that while a valid ParentTree Stream ref does mean that it is in a non-page stream, an invalid one no longer implies a page stream. It is possible that marks were made and a key created, but the content stream subsequently was dropped. These should be excluded from the /StructElem /K entries (as the marks don't really exist) and the ParentTree can just not emit the index. So there should be a signal to the ParentTree Stream entries that they have been emitted (and if to a non-page content stream its ref).

subject: Add /StructParents to FormXObjects for tagged PDF
message:
Currently the assumption is that all marks are on Page streams. It appears the purpose of this change is to also properly export marks on FormXObject streams. However, this means that the mark needs to remember where it came from (currently this is by recording the page number) and emit something like
```
<</Type /MCR
/Pg 2 0 R %optional, overrides outer /Pg
/Stm 4 0 R %Stream containing marked-content sequence (eg, FormXObject)
/MCID 0 %Marked-content identifier (in the Stm)
>>
```
in order to point the structure element at the right child marks. See ISO 32000-2:2020﻿ 14.7.5.2 Marked-content sequences as content items Example 5.

subject: Support reverse font and font family lookup for Variable Fonts
message:
So while it might be a good idea to adjust the family and font after applying the variation, this has never been an issue here because this is simply creating an SkTypeface from data. There should be nothing particularly interesting about the "family" at this point. The question I have which does not appear answered elsewhere is "What does this newly adjusted SkTypeface do differently from the previously un-adjusted SkTypeface that makes a difference?"

In particular it appears that the `fDWriteFontFamily` is only ever used to get family names. Is the issue is that Chromium is using SkTypfaces made from data to lookup family names and do matching? That would be strange. In general, there is no really good reason a typeface made from data should really have a family or family names and at the very least they should not be trusted (at the very least the is nothing unique about them, they're only useful for display to the user).

As far as `fDWriteFont` it looks like it is only dragged around now to get the PostScript name, but even there we should now be using the font face for that now.

subject: Support reverse font and font family lookup for Variable Fonts
message:
It is quite unfortunate that only FontConfig exposes a "strong match" vs "weak match" bit when doing matching. Chromium shouldn't be doing a check against family names but against the strength of the match when doing the request against the collection.

In some ways what is being done here would be nice to do as part of the `bestMatch` logic. However, writing that logic out here would be both complex and not necessarily always match the logic used by DirectWrite to pick the "font" and "family". So this is fine.

subject: Stop counting on sources_assignment_filters in gn/utils.gni.
message:
While this is a fine CL, we're not counting on sources_assignment_filters to be set here (and the //skia:skia target uses skia_utils_sources) and the Skia build explicitly sets sources_assignment_filters to empty anyway.

What's really going on is that all of the files here are always in the build, but internally each .cpp file listed (and many of the .h files) has a big '#ifdef SK_BUILD_FOR_XXX' block around most of the contents. So the files can always 'build' on all platforms. (And this is how the Chromium build is currently working with the sources_assignment_filter set to nothing in the Chromium //skia target.)

So in a CL like this we would also want to remove all of those '#ifdef SK_BUILD_FOR_XXX' blocks at the same time to make sure we're always using one mechanism or the other. There's been some debate about which way to go on this. On the one hand it's clean to have the build state which files get built and avoid building files which won't contribute symbols to the build. On the other hand, having all the files listed means that they will end up in generated project files so they can always be found and considered part of the project (even if they don't actually contribute to the current target platform, we really want to be able to flag particular sources as part of a project but not part of the build).  Maybe there's some clever way to do that...

So what is being passed around here isn't really a "simulations" but a "here is a bunch of information on how to re-create the font I wanted". In general this would want to be a type with a typeface factory id (or some id so the format of the data is known) and an sk_sp<SkData>.

If this where all Chromium side I would say land this all and we'll fix it up later. However, this being on the Skia side I'd like to make sure we get this at least somewhat logically correct first.

message:
So for CoreText we would need an opaque bit of data for sure, but after a lot of thinking it seems synthetic bold and oblique should probably be called out directly since in theory FontConfig typefaces can specify synthetic bold and it is possible that other backends could also offer such synthetics. The other existing parameters aren't really that different, one can specify a bunch of variation axis locations for font data that doesn't have any axes or even to a backend that doesn't support them at all.

Also, we do want this to get plumbed through serialization. And cloning. And some testing. So I went and did https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1148216 .

subject: Support simulations in DWriteTypeface's MakeFromStream
message:

Also, this is related to the issues around being able to deserialize typeface data properly on the receiving end. Like with the CoreText hvgl format issues (where CoreText will create them as system fonts but not from data) where it becomes necessary to serialize into a different format. In this case the issue is the the format is "mostly standard" but with "extra implementation bits" on the side.

subject: Modernize SkFontMgr_Mac::onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter
message:
If one passes in a family name and that gets a (real) hit, then even just the `CTFontCreateForString` will match style.

However, passing in `nullptr` or otherwise ending up with a "default font" will do fallback but not apply the style (possibly because the somewhat magic "default font" doesn't really have any styles other than default). Making a copy with style attributes still doesn't dislodge this "default font with no styles" bit and the style doesn't change.

subject: Modernize SkFontMgr_Mac::onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter
message: Turns out the "bit" was that the CTFontDescriptor set the kFontName (the PostScript name) so nothing else would match. Instead this replaces that with a kFontFamilyName match. This is not at all what is desired, but after reading through a lot of CoreText documentation and trying various things it looks like this may be the best work-around for this inherit limitation of the API.

subject: Modernize SkFontMgr_Mac::onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter

subject: Add const to SkData in SkTypeface_fontations API
message:
While `sk_sp<const Foo>` or any `const Foo` where `Foo : public SkRefCnt` is fine but should always be redundant, which is why we often don't. That is to say, if a class has an intrusive thread safe reference count it should already by externally const to be thread safe. So, yeah, `const` here is correct, it's just annoying that the default is mutable so `const` is all noisy and in one's face.

That being said, `SkData` does have non-const methods for construction purposes, so this might be fine.

If this is a crusade to make as many `sk_sp<Foo>` into `sk_sp<const Foo>` as possible, that's fine, just wanted to note that this wasn't already the case due to the visual noise of the extra `const` (which should be implicit) when the classes should always be logically const anyway after construction / initialization (before the first additional reference escapes).

subject: Remove misleading consts from function parameters
message:
Can we not do things like this? Yes, the `const` on a parameter means nothing to the declaration (the user of the function). However, these are all definitions as well, and the `const` on the parameter is the same as putting a `const` on a local variable. As someone implementing / reading / maintaining this code the `const` signals intent that the implementation shouldn't be changing the values, thereby reducing the mental burden. It is unfortunate that the syntax doesn't allow for an inline definition to distinguish between these two kinds of `const` directly, though one could do so by writing a pure declaration first and a definition after it to be explicit.

Most of the linked article doesn't really apply here, and the [bit that does apply](https://quuxplusone.github.io/blog/2019/01/03/const-is-a-contract/#i-looked-for-this-kind-of-typo-i) simply shows that one can write incorrect code.

subject: Improve simple containers
message:
The primary motivation for this is to add the move constructor for `AutoSTArray`, `trim_to`, and `kCount`. The other changes are right now for consistency and ease of testing.

In particular, `trim_to` and `kCount` allow for the user to "allocate" the whole storage (using `kCount`) to make it legal to pass the storage into interfaces which can optimistically take a buffer and fill it out if it is big enough (always returning the size of the buffer needed) and then use `trim_to` to shrink the allocation if necessary.

subject: Improve simple containers
message:
Ah, naming things.

`folly::small_vector` uses `MaxInline` but doesn't seems to expose it.

`eastl::fixed_vector` uses `kMaxSize` and is somewhat misleading.

`kNumPreallocatedObjects` isn't right because no objects are preallocated (just the space for them).

`kPreallocatedCount` isn't bad since it goes along with the documentation, but the documentation is bad. The storage isn't really "preallocated" it's just inline, like `std::optional` where the specification uses the term `nested within`. Also, it isn't "on the Stack".

Note that the template parameter is named `kCountRequested`, so the current name of just `kCount` makes sense since it's the actual count one ended up with. If we change this name the template name might want to be updated to `kInlineCountRequested`?

Also, while it seems like this name should be more descriptive doing so would probably just be verbose. What else could `kCount` even be referring to here? Obviously not the runtime count. The only other count is the `kCountRequested` and so we know it goes with that.

I would prefer to use the standard term "size" instead of "count" but there's a lot of "count" going on here already.

In the end I'm leaning toward leaving these as is. This is an internal only type so if we find it confusing in the future we can always change it. However, I will update the documentation comment.

subject: Fix Android NDK FontMgr alias scanning
message:
While this does work and fixes many tests in Chromium when attempting to use the this font manager, it fails when running on Android 15 and 16. While this does work and is a correct way to do the comparison, on Android 15 and 16 `AFont_getAxis*` are no longer useful as only the single most default member of a family is reported. On Android 14 and below `ASystemFontIterator_next` would report an entry for each listing in xml file, but in 15 and 16 it will only report one member for each font file from each family.

subject: [pdf] Unpremul after interpolating unpremul
message:
The one difficulty with this is it will make almost every gradient with a non-opaque color stop that Chromium currently produces a Type1 (Function based) shader. CSS unfortunately spec'ed gradient interpolation to be in premul, which means there is no way to create a gradient from transparent blue to opaque red, for example, so Chromium is always requesting interpolation in premul. In addition to being slower to compute, Poppler has some issues with applying the matrix and pdf.js just doesn't support them (draws pink). Reader, Pdfium, and Preview are all fine with this though.

Unfortunately, the overall function to interpolate in premul and then unpremul is not linear, which seems to force being function based.

subject: [pdf] Unpremul after interpolating unpremul
message: On the one hand putting the unpremul step here would avoid `roll`s but it would mean duplicating the unpremul code for every interval, which could be very costly in code size.

subject: [pdf] Unpremul after interpolating unpremul
message: After some experimentation, it appears Preview (pdfkit) really doesn't like this `eq`.

subject: [pdf] Unpremul after interpolating unpremul
message:
When finished interpolating in premul the values left on the stack should look like the following, where `rgb0`,`a0` is the (initial, unpremultiplied) color at the beginning of a range and `rgb1`,`a1` is the (initial, unpremultiplied) color at the end of the range, and `t` is how far along that range the point is (all values 0 to 1).

```((rgb1*a1-rgb0*a0)*t+rgb0*a0)/((a1-a0)*t+a0)```

The initial `rgb*a` premuls are done ahead of time. The `rgb` and `a` are interpolated, the `rgb/a` is done and the `a` is discarded (will be provided by the transparency mask shader).

subject: Make skslc use Tint built from CMake instead of GN rules
message:
It turns out that `ninja -tdeps` on a target only works if there was a `depfile` for that target. This is generally the case for our compile actions, but for most other targets it isn't. So generally one would need to use `ninja -tdeps <target>` to get the dynamic dependencies of a target (add those, if any), then use `ninja -tinputs <target>` to get the list of inputs (add those) and the recurse on the inputs.

When `ninja -tdeps` is used at the top level one gets effectively the result of evaluating this recursively, since the output is the concatenation of everything done in a build. Unfortunately, `ninja` doesn't seem to have a tool to just do this recursive lookup for any given target directly.

I'd like to get this right because this might end up being a model for how Skia should shell out to build other things as well.

subject: Update clang and iwyu for Linux
message:
To summarize the vulkan header issue with the layering check...

`//src/gpu/ganesh/vk:ganesh_vulkan` depends on `@vulkan_headers//:vulkan_headers` and expects to get vulkan headers from there. However, `//src/gpu/ganesh/vk:ganesh_vulkan` also depends on `//src/gpu/vk:vk` which depends on `//include/third_party/vulkan:vulkan`. So both sets of vulkan headers end up in the include path and in this failing case the preprocessor finds the one in the indirect dependency instead of the direct dependency and the modules system complains.

subject: Update clang and iwyu for Linux
message:
What we really want (yet again) is `implementation_deps`. The flag `--experimental_cc_implementation_deps` defaults to true starting with Bazel 7.0. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20098 for discussion. With this we can have the internal targets depend on the internal vulkan headers but not re-export the include path.

Interestingly, the way G3 gets around this is by banning `include` attributes outside of `third_party` (and so all includes are absolute and you can't even express "sometimes this include comes from here and sometimes from over there" which triggers this issue). Since G3 "doesn't have this problem" `implementation_deps` hasn't gotten a lot of internal support which seems to be why it is taking so long to be able to use. Even though anything that isn't a monorepo really needs it.

In any event, we can now use `implementation_deps` and are now using them after https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/898139 .

subject: Update clang and iwyu for Linux
message:
So unfortunately this IWYU version has regressions.

In particular it doesn't appear to see the types used though a pointer deduced from a structured binding as a "use". This leads it to think SkGlyph only needs to be forward declared when it really needs to be defined in a number of locations.

There is also something going on with use of types that result from templates, which may be related since structured bindings use a similar deduction.

Then there is a potential "progression" which to us is a regression. IWYU is now suggesting that a number of includes instead be forward declarations in the cpp files generated from header files. The reason for this is that the types declared in the cpp file should not "escape" and the header file itself doesn't use the types it declares. So IWYU is correct in the sense that the header file compiled in its own TU doesn't need the full definitions. However, any use of that header as a header will require full definitions (as the declarations in headers are in some sense "public" which the declarations in cpp files are in some sense "private").

subject: Optional PathOps
message:
I'm going to more strongly object to this entire approach, as I have in the past. The code in pdf/ and xps/ logically cannot exist outside of libskia. These work by implementing SkDevice and (must) use a ridiculous number of internal types which will never (or at least should never) be public. The pdf/ and xps/ code, if used, must be in the skia target. For example this CL passes the "Shared" builds simply by making it impossible to create an official (or any) shared build of pdf/ and xps/ at all (either in libskia.so or on their own). In fact it seems this change makes it impossible (especially for outside users of Skia) to build pdf/ and xps/ in the GN build unless statically linking Skia. Linkers do not enforce any visibility on static objects. (The Bazel build also has this problem. Looking more closely it looks like the Bazel build of Skia is extremely antagonistic to producing any form of shared objects.)

The proper way to do any of this is to make an interface for pathops and make it plug-able. Even if there is only ever one implementation this is still what needs to be done. Either that or we need to remove the use of pathops from pdf/ and xps/.

Or we publicly state that Skia's build will no longer support building shared objects (which would be compatible with the Bazel build), that the Skia build will produce only static libraries, and then the user (and maybe a Skia side helper) can gather up all these static libraries into a libskia shared library? This is essentially just acknowledging the "big ball of mud". Internally everything can have full visibility into everything else (because the linker does not enforce visibility on static libraries), but can still be separate targets. This is essentially what the Bazel build is doing (Bazel enforces through its own "visibility", not linker visibility), except we could make it useful by then having a "skia library" target which pulls in a bunch of static libraries and builds a shared library out of them (at which point the linker will finally export the visibility information). This is more or less what the GN //:skia component is, except assembled from source_set instead of static_library. Doing something like this would allow a change like this to land without breaking users who want pdf/ in a libskia.so, and would also allow Skia to stuff the "modules" in there as well (since none of them are actually independent) and would allow the "modules" to end up in the final shared Skia library.

subject: Optional PathOps

subject: Reland "move pathops into a module"
message:
What even is the point of "modules" at this point? As far as I can tell it's just a setup which makes it impossible to make a useful shared build. There will never be an effort to make them only depend only on SK_API or even SK_SPI, so they're all just part of the big ball of mud anyway. What is gained with all of this over just having a `//:pathops` (which depends on `//:skia`) target that `//:skia` doesn't directly depend on, but `//:pdf` and `//:xps` do depend on only when enabled?

If the idea is to be able to build core Skia with an external "libpathops" then the first thing that needs to be done is write an interface. Then `//:pdf` and `//:xps` could be updated to use that interface and then the build of such a thing (internal or external) can be handled separately (push the "linking" to runtime). The alternative to doing this is to actually do the work of making these actually modules (only depend on SK_API or SK_SPI) so that one can create a bunch of shared objects. "Pretending" like this is only going to lead to lots of issues.

So no, this doesn't seem all that reasonable.

subject: Make sure inline static symbols in headers are visible
message:
So the idea here is that all of these end up declaring some static object in a header. If any of these headers end up in more than one TU there will be a definition in each TU of them. When linking happens the linker will pick one. However, if these TUs end up linked into different shared objects then there will be multiple of them.

The solution here seems to be to mark all of these as publicly visible to allow the dynamic linker to pick one from among the shared objects. On the other hand, Skia, as a library, would really like to minimize the number of exported symbols.

Looking at these, it seems that in all cases it would make more sense to move these definitions into the TUs. (This is a little tricky for the one macro, which will need to be split into a "declare" and a "define".) For some of these it might be considered to just move define of the global into the TU, but it doesn't look like that's really necessary for perf in any of these.

subject: Allow generateMetrics to also generate path
message:
`SkPath` is 16 bytes on a 64 bit system (it is more or less a pointer / reference to a `SkPathRef` and a few cached properties) and is generally treated like a value type. At the moment this could consume the ref and it would avoid an extra (though very local) ref/unref pair. At that point it might be worth doing value semantics here (allowing the caller to make the decision) though that will probably end up with a few extra reads/writes on the stack.

Except that `SkPath` is not currently move-able! This is because of the `std::atomic` members it has. There is an ongoing process to try to fix this (make `SkPath` immutable and introduce a `SkPathBuilder`) but that will take some time. So we could write `std::move` here but at the moment the copy assignment operator is still being called anyway. It's probably still useful as a marker of intent and means things would work better once `SkPath` is moveable though. But this does currently discourage value type usage here.

subject: Should we return early if the matrix inversion fails?
message:
The logic behind this change appears to be that if `invert` returns `false` then `inverse` is not changed, and so remains the identity matrix. Any stroking and path effect would then be incorrectly applied to `localPath` (and the assigned to `devPath`), which does look like a problem since the zero area fill may no longer be zero area when it should have been. However, that work is currently discarded as `SkGlyph::setPath` will only allow the path to be set once. After this `setPath` call the one below will be a no-op (and will return `false`). So logically one might as well return here since any work being done below will be discarded.

Another possible way to handle this would be to recognize that if the matrix cannot be inverted then the path returned should take up no area and simply be considered empty. However, that is not true if stroking with hairline, so if we return early here we also need to set `hairline` to `true` here if needed. However, this isn't currently being handled correctly since `hairline` will be set to the correct value below (too late). Arguably this `if` block should go below the hairline `if` block below, but before the commit of `localPath` to `devPath`, though that still isn't quite correct.

Really we need some test cases where there is a singular and a near singular matrix used on a glyph and an SkPath of the glyph outline with various path effects and stroke widths and ensure that they act the same. Is there any specific scenario that motivated this proposed change?

Part of the issue here is that logically the stroking (other than hairline) and the path effect should be done to the outline down in the scaler context before the matrix is applied, and to a post-hinted but pre-matrix glyph outline, which isn't really possible. This code is trying to do that "in post" but this breaks down when the matrix cannot be inverted.

subject: [fontations] Set font format in onGetAdvancedMetrics
message:
It seems really awkward to introduce a fontations_ffi enum here that lists font types like Type1 that aren't supported. `SkAdvancedTypefaceMetrics::FontType` is really a bit silly of a name, it's more like a `SkPDF::FontType` with very specific meanings related to how PDF viewers will treat the font data. In other words the Skia side enum isn't really about the font format but more about what we think PDF viewers will support. The names are deceptively generic because we're pretending like there isn't this very tight coupling between these `FontType` enum values and PDF viewer implementations, but that's the way things are. The reality is that the format checking would be better done in the PDF code by having a separate parser and validator for the bits there, but that's a pain so the hack is to ask the typeface and essentially push a bit of PDF logic into every typeface implementation because that is more expedient.

Also, this doesn't need to be fast in any way. This is only used by printing and the result is cached.

subject: [Fontations] Protect path retrieval arrays with lock
message:
The issue here appears to be that this is being called from an SkDrawable (SkFontationsScalerContext::generateDrawable::ColrGlyphDrawable to drawCOLRGlyph) which could be called from more that one thread, as well as being called in the "normal" single thread way.

In general SkScalerContexts are single thread, but in this case `generateDrawable` allowed a reference to leak out into the wild, so whatever that SkDrawable needs to do needs to be thread safe.

subject: [Fontations] Protect path retrieval arrays with lock
message: A note to any future visitors: What happened here is that the strikes are "prepared" within a lock with the intention that the strike and its scaler context are only mutable within that lock (by locking and unlocking the strike). However, the actual drawing of the paths or strikes is done outside that lock. Using the masks, paths, or drawables is assumed to be thread safe (since it is supposed to be read only to use them). These shared objects are accessible because a reference to the strike is being held. So while the the mutable parts of the scaler context and strike are only called single threaded, the "thread safe" and "read only" results (including SkDrawables) need to be thread safe.

subject: SkScalerContext to not own SkTypeface
message:
Yes. So the way the system works, the SkStrike/SkScalerContexts are held by the SkStrikeCache. When a user uses an SkTypeface the unique id of the SkTypeface is used to lookup an exisiting SkStrike/SkScalerContext in the SkStrikeCache (or used to create a new SkStrike/SkScalerContext if there isn't one already). What this change is taking advantage of is that the SkScalerContext can only ever be used (created or pulled out of the strike cache) if the user provides the corresponding SkTypeface as part of the call. As a result there is no reason for the SkScalerContext to own a reference to the SkTypeface as the SkTypeface must still be alive for the SkScalerContext to be created or found in the cache. If the SkStrikeCache contains an Sk5trike/SkScalerContext associated with an SkTypeface and the user drops all references to that SkTyepface then the SkScalerContxt will have a dangling reference to that SkTypeface. However, it is no longer possible to reach that SkScalerContext in the strike cache, except to delete that SkScalerContext when it is purged from the strike cache and the delete does not need the SkTypeface reference.

To make this sort of thing more obvious, we can create an even larger change where each SkScalerContext method takes the SkTypeface by reference and everything is updated for this. Unfortunatly, due to the runtime virtual proxy support this is complicated. In the end we do want to move toward moving the reference out of SkScalerContext and instead pass the value to the methods (essentially as an additional "this"). However, with full proxy support the SkScalerContext will need four "this" parameters (the regular implicit "this", the top level proxy in the current SkScalerContext proxy chain, the assocaited implementation SkTypeface (the one that created this SkScalerContext) and the top level proxy in the current SkTypeface proxy chain.

All that to say, yes this is "safe" and needs to be done, but also there is an even bigger change that needs to happen after this.

subject: Build fixes for QNX aarch64.
message:
float32x4_t vrndnq_f32(float32x4_t a): Floating-point Round to Integral, to nearest with ties to even (vector). 

It looks like the only difference here is that while `vrndns_f32` is an intrisic documented by ARM, there is no instruction for it.

I do need to point out that the complaint here is that `vrndns_f32` isn't available in GCC 8.3.0, however it is in GCC 8.5.0 (GCC commmit 852423cd68b403d09a14f6436080243c609a57a8). It seems rather unfotunate to make this kind of change when a minor version compiler update fixed this issue (and presumably many more). That being said, I suppose we've been trying to support Firefox which currently claims to support GCC 8.1, it seems strange that this issue hasn't come up there.

Note that GCC 8 was the first to support C++17 and we're currently trying to drop support for GCC 8 so we can move to C++20 (which means at least GCC 10, though maybe 11).

subject: Build fixes for QNX aarch64.
Build fixes for QNX aarch64.
message:
GCC
```
  movi v1.4s, 0
  ins v1.s[0], v0.s[0]
  frintn v1.4s, v1.4s
  fcvtzu w0, s1
  ret
```
Clang
```
  movi v1.2d, #0000000000000000
  mov v1.s[0], v0.s[0]
  frintn v0.4s, v1.4s
  fcvtzu w0, s0
  ret
```

So even with optimizations, this does pay the extra price of the splat. Not sure how much difference that makes. Mostly I was interested in seeing if, after optimizations, there was even a difference. It appears that the compiler doesn't see through the vector instruction and see that the effect of the `mov`s are being discarded.

subject: Initial move to refactor PathOps
message:
As much as possible we want to move away from any form of "registration" / "global" to set. This has run into huge issues with using Skia as a library as any global makes it more difficult for a library to use Skia (at the moment it is really only possible to use Skia from application code).

In other words, we really do just want an interface and then have an object of an implementation of that interface passed in from the user of Skia.

subject: Initial move to refactor PathOps
message: If we're going through all this work to rename everything, why not make pathops an interface? Even if for the first pass we just always create a new one (of a specific implementation type, with no state) and then call the method on it. In other words, why this rename which leaves everything static? SkPathOps is currently set up like the old SkFontHost and what we want is an interface more like SkFontMgr.

subject: Initial move to refactor PathOps

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message:
Unfortunately, it appears this is never useful.

If we do this, we bake the scale into the descriptor, which means we're just resizing everything just to scale it back down but without any benefit of de-duplication.

Really what we wanted was to de-duplicate all the textSize + pathEffect that can be scaled to be identical. But the textSize changing means the pathEffect will be applied at a different path and so that isn't a scale, and if the pathEffect changes we don't know anything about how it works internally, so we don't know if that scales.

The stroke is a kind of special path effect that we do know how it works internally and so we can just scale its parameters here. But the parameters for the path effect are already baked in.

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message: Unfortunately, it appears this turns A8 into images instead of masks, which means blurs are always "black".

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message: When this is `d0` that means "specifies its own colors". We want `d1` "specifies shape but not colors". Reader and Preview seem to be letting the current color leak through anyway. Pdfium does not, but changing just this doesn't appear to be enough to get the color through. If we remove the graphics state with the SMask then the rectangle does draw red. The specification does call out in the documentation for `d1` that images shouldn't be used, but image masks are acceptable but it doesn't directly address SMasks.

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message: Opened https://crbug.com/362796158 for Pdfium. However, Preview is also quite poor at handling SMasks in Type3 fonts (it's also not all that great at handling SMasks anywhere else). If it were only Reader this change to push the mask filters into the Type3 glyphs would be a great size improvement (though sometimes the blur gets a bit pixelated when scaled up a lot, really want to force bi-linear on that to smooth it out). However, we may just need to punt on mask filters for now until the viewers can be fixed.

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message:
Because it makes the final PDF smaller.

It is possible to make this A8 and then use SkPDFGraphicState::kAlpha_SMaskMode, but in PDF this means emitting a black image and an SMask with the alpha in it. Instead here we just emit a single channel image and use SkPDFGraphicState::kLuminosity_SMaskMode which means we can emit a single channel image without a separate SMask image.

The existing code was actually incorrect in that it always produced black text (it was never shaded with the current color) but it was also almost never used (it would only be used on bi-level bitmap only fonts). The approach here (kGray and kLuminosity) is what SkPDFDevice::internalDrawPathWithFilter does, which is how this was (kind of) handled previously.

subject: [pdf] Reduce drawing glyphs as paths
message:
This is incorrect. This was written under the impression that the `miter-limit` value is a limit on how far the miter can extend (the `miter-length`). However, this is not the case as `miter-limit = miter-length / stroke-width`. Since this is already a ratio (and `stroke-width` is being scaled) this value should not be scaled. This resulted in https://issues.chromium.org/issues/379510433 . Part of this is the terrible documentation around the miter limit and what it does.

Created https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/946917 to fix.

subject: Remove unnecessary const qualifiers from single char params
message: I very dislike changes like these. Removing the `const` from declarations that are not definitions is fine (they don't mean anything), but removing the `const` from defintions is terrible. As a maintainer I want all locals (including parameters) to be marked `const` unless there is a need to do otherwise so there is less need to keep track of potential state.

subject: Remove unnecessary const qualifiers from single char params
message:
I'm sure Clang Tidy comlained about this one because it is a declaration and not a definition. The rest of these changes are not consistent, the other changes are removing `const` from a definition, which is quite different.

I'm not a big fan of removing `const` from declarations to begin with even if they don't actually mean anything. But we really should not be removing `const` from definitions.

message:
May be a larger issue, but it appears that Skia currently blanket adds

C and C++
-Wno-attributes
-Wno-deprecated-declarations
-Wno-maybe-uninitialized
-Wno-psabi
-Wno-switch-default
-Wno-unused-parameter
-Wno-unreachable-code

Some of these may or may not still be needed, but in the case of `-Wno-attributes` this is due to the fact that while `__has_attribute` now exists so we can test if `no_sanitize` exists, because the warning is about the string inside we cannot test for support for that (arguably this attribute should have been split up into many `no_sanitize_foo` attributes so they could be individually detected).

subject: Add SK_NO_SANITIZE_CFI that has effect when building with Clang
message:
I see that Skia in WebKit is being compiled with [`-Wno-attributes`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/13710089bc1a5a0c079f1e58404d62e7c94ce81d/Source/ThirdParty/skia/CMakeLists.txt#L1046C5-L1046C20) the issue being that `SkTArray.h` is (terribly) in `include/private` so is being compiled in translation units that depend on Skia, requiring this issue to be fixed (otherwise all downstream users of Skia must also use `-Wno-attributes`). So `SkVx.h` could use (and probably should have used) `SK_NO_SANITIZE("cfi")` instead of the as-hoc `#if` and it would be fine since it is in `src/`.

More frustrating here is that this particular case is about SkCanvas::Layer having an STArray, but SkCanvas::Layer is only ever used in private implementation details and doesn't even need to be a complete type in the header (except that C++ syntax makes it rather ugly for it not to be).

In any event, this (at Patch Set 4) is a fine short term fix for this issue.

subject: Fix style and axis scanning for variable fonts
message:
No, this is an unrelated fix for an existing issue. The issue is that the font scanning on the FreeType side has been calculating the wrong variation and style for named instances for some time. Instead of the variation and style based on the named instance it is instead always based on the default instance. The variation part of this was partially covered up by `SkTypeface_FreeType::FaceRec::setupAxes` ignoring the requested variation if a named instance were requested (on the original theory that specifying a named instance this way essentially made it "not variable" anymore, though we think of them less this way now). However, the style was incorrectly computed as pointed out by the now resurrected `fontmgr_FontConfigInterface_tests`.

This also points out that everything here is calling the scanner too often, though it looks like we might be able to clean that up after AndroidNDK, FCI, and Fuchsia are updated.

Also, this also points out that this whole `SkFontScanner` interface is only good for FreeType and Fontations. It cannot be made to work with DirectWrite and CoreText. For the future we will need an interface which takes some font data and returns a collection of typefaces (or proto-typefaces) as DirectWrite does not expose instance indexes and CoreText does not expose ttc indexes or instance indexes. In general it may be required to get rid of the idea of ttc index and named index and instead have the lookup be by postscript name (at least internally) as I believe is the current proposal on the web standards side.

subject: Disable strict aliasing for PartitionAlloc in Skia
message: At the very least, this is incorrect. "Strict aliasing" (or just glvalue access rules C++20 7.2.1.11, note that the rules in C++ are somewhat different than C, such as not making `unsigned char` special) is just how C and C++ work, breaking these rules produces undefined behavior. The use of `-fno-strict-aliasing` is to instead use a non-standard dialect of C or C++ (and one which isn't super well defined). Compiler optimizations are a completely separate issue.

subject: Disable strict aliasing for PartitionAlloc in Skia
message: In other words, this comment should read more like "PartitionAlloc (and possibly other projects) isn't written in C or C++ but in a dialect that assumes pointers of different types (other than `char` or `unsigned char`) may freely point to the same locations in memory."

subject: [pdf] Change structure identifiers to match specification
message:
This change does makes it very obvious that this hasn't been doing anything and always returning -1 since [[pdf] Properly handle drawing not on a page](https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/909cf06ad73879d1d247bd58572c60c1bfabe7ba). The issue being that `createStructParentKeyForElemId` is checking to see if we are currently on a page (if there is an `fPageDevice`) but the caller of this method `SkPDFDocument::onEndPage` did `fPageDevice = nullptr` right before making the call. So link annotations did not point back at their structure elements.

To be correct the annotations need to be added when there really is an active page, since the annotations are tied to the active page.

subject: [pdf] Emit correct tag for marked-content items
message: The implementation of the new `SkPDFStructTree::Mark::structType` and the existing `SkPDFStructElem::emitStructElem` need to agree on the structure type. This is a required field and must be a name (like `/Name`) so cannot be empty. Previously we just let this be empty and the one real user (`emitStructElem`) would emit `NonStruct` on empty. Instead of spreading out a bunch of logic to keep things in sync, just use `NonStruct` here instead and don't allow `fStructType` to be the empty string. To avoid having lots of copies of this `NonStruct` string in memory just hold onto one so that all the SkString copies point at the same data under the hood (since SkString is copy on write).

subject: [pdf] Emit correct tag for marked-content items
message:
Hmmmm... SkString is already 8 bytes, it's really an `sk_sp<SkString::Rec>`. I suppose this could potentially save a ref and unref (which are basically never contended). Earlier there was a version of this which could return a new empty SkString which couldn't be returned by reference, but now that isn't happening due to fixing the struct type logic and asserting that there is an active structure element instead.

That being said, there is just one caller which requires a value and it will just be moved multiple times down into the union, it will be emitted, and then destructed. This would need to happen anyway, so it doesn't currently change anything.

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message: I think this is a bad idea. Nothing should migrate to SkPathBuilder as it means we will be stuck with yet another thing that cannot be migrated to.

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message:
And migrating to SkPathBuilder also isn't a migration, because there is no immutable SkPath so it doesn't matter because you haven't caught where the mutations happen. And in the process we now have two builders. Removing the existing SkPathBuilder, re-naming the existing SkPath as SkPathBuilder with an alias to SkPath, with a new immutable interface SkPath available with a build flag (for finding where SkPath is being used mutably) is the only real way forward.

So far I've been defensive here. However, I do believe that doing this CL is a huge net negative for Skia as a whole. I would need overwhelming evidence that this approach can actually be made to work across all users and allow them a migration path this isn't an immediate all-or-nothing. And this really does mean all users and not just a little bit here or there.

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message:
I should add more details of why to b/335431546, but what this boils down to is SkPath is already a mutable path builder, we don't need another mutable path builder. What we need is an immutable path object.

The current name of SkPath is actually just a misnomer, it is actually a mutable path builder that we then attempt to use like an immutable path. This is a holdover from when Skia was thread antagonistic and didn't really handle threading at all.

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message: I spent three days attempting to see if Chrome, Android, and G3 could be moved to SkPathBuilder by adding things missing to SkPathBuilder. The answer is absolutely not. It would be required to make SkPathBuilder exactly the same as SkPath for at least some period of time in order to do the migration without being able to do an enormous all-at-once change across all the repos. There is no means to incrementally move to the current SkPathBuilder.

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message: No, this is just more tech debt and more future work. Everything about SkPathBuilder is a dead end because we cannot migrate to it (without it being SkPath).

subject: SkPathBuilder tweaks
message: To be clear, to migrate to SkPathBuilder would be to simply make it the current SkPath.

subject: Emit StructElem ID only when referenced
message:
Using https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/irregular/ (which has properly marked up headers) and printing from Chrome this does emit an IDTree with just the needed (referenced) IDs. When there are no referenced IDs then no IDTree or IDs are emitted.

That being said, at PS1 this still doesn't seem quite right. Really we want the node ids to be marked as used when the annotation is emitted (the references are actually emitted) as it is possible for the user to describe these things but then end up never emitting them (like when creating the structure tree for a whole site, but only printing some pages into the pdf).

subject: Emit StructElem ID only when referenced
message:
So at patch set 1 this is somewhat using the wrong approach. The approach in patch set 1 is to add back in any StructElem if its ID is referenced from any emitted attribute's ID list.

Instead, this should, right before emitting the structure element tree, run through all the attributes which are to be emitted and look at the IDs in their lists. If the ID references a StructElem which is to be emitted (has a mark or is otherwise non-discardable) then we leave that ID in the attribute list and mark the StructElem node as needing to emit its ID. Otherwise (when the node relating to the ID in the attribute's ID list can be discarded) then that ID should be removed from the list (as it references something with no marks anywhere).

subject: Emit StructElem ID only when referenced
message: If an attribute references a StructElem ID which has no marks, that's not really enough reason to remove that StructElem (and its ID) as even if nothing is drawn for row or column headers it still makes sense to keep the structure. So what we want is to ensure that for any attribute that is emitted, any IDs it uses mark the target (and its parents) as no-discard and marks the target to emit the ID. Of course, this could cause attributes which were discardable to no longer be discardable, so this process would need to continue until nothing new is found.

subject: Add stub Fontations SkTypeface backend
message:
This is fine for now.

A number of the SkFontMgr implementations that just work with font file data (FontConfig and DirectWrite) could in theory work with any SkTypeface implementation that can create from file data (e.g. Lookup fonts with DirectWrite font collection but instantiate as FreeType or Fontations). CoreText is generally written antagonistically to such an arrangement, but could be made to work, maybe. In any event, it's a good excuse to start separating SkFontMgr into SkFontCollection and the typeface factories, and allowing the SkFontCollections to optionally take a typeface factory.

The only real difficulty with splitting the collection from its preferred typeface factory (like using FontConfig with something other than FreeType) is that the collection may contain fonts that don't work with other factories, but in theory that can also be somewhat worked around.

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message:
We set the font manager here for the same reason we want to pass the text shaping around, which was to get off the build time settings and globals. However, now we're at the point where this concept is more general than just sending in a font manager, we also want to logically send in more text handling stuff here, in a kind of `TextProvider` which would include the SkFontMgr, SkShaper, SkUnicode, and whatever else is needed for text like things. Note that one of the primary reasons to pass the SkFontMgr here is to use it to call SkShaper::MakeFontMgrRunIterator which could also be a thing on SkShapers::Factory (a `makeFontRunIterator`). However, Skottie also uses this SkFontMgr as a way to try to look up named fonts for finding the initial typeface, so it is used for slightly more than that.

The proposal here is to add an additional SkShapers::Factory parameter, but the concern is the extra plumbing. This should have the same plumbing as the current font manager plumbing, so another way to do this is replace the font manager here with a new type that contains a font manager and these new factory callbacks. Another way would be to take everything that would go on that type and instead put it into ResourceProvider and have the font manager from the resource provider be preferred to the one passed here until this one can be removed.

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message:
I would prefer for Skia not to have any mutable globals at all (and if it does need "globals" for them to go on a "library" object which stores all the library state and the user sets up and passes back in, like `FT_Library` or something like that (though even this is to be avoided if possible).

Mutable globals on a library make it very difficult to use properly, for case studies see `strtok` vs `strtok_r`, using any call in the C standard library that uses the current locale, etc. It's fine for an application to have these, but a Skia shouldn't have them.

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message: Yeah, and that's fine if you just live in G3 or just live in Chromium (in which case you don't have to be a library, you're just application code as a source bundle). But Skia should be a library. This isn't just a little bit of "dislike", it's more like "you should be this tall to ride this ride". Skia is frankly a bit of an embarrassment here as even things like FontConfig came kicking and screaming into the "libraries should not have globals" world years ago.

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message:
Well, then at least `lib2` is going to need to pass something in to indicate how to do text shaping, in the same way it's going to need to pass in a `ResourceProvider`. In fact, maybe it would be better to add all of this to `ResourceProvider` instead? (Or something like it, which is essentially that this CL currently is.) In addition to loading named assets we need a way to provide text shaping implementations.

Also G3 gets away with many sins, as no one there writes libraries. Which is also why Skia hasn't been a library (it's just a source dump of application code that one can compile into an application).

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message:
SkGraphics is a big offender that we eventually need to do away with. That should all be in a `SkLibrary` that users need to pass back in if they need to. Though it's possible that `Init` may be ok since it's mostly tied to architecture.

Skottie and SVG don't need any of this if they just hard depend on certain SkShaper and SkUnicode implementation targets, the same way they don't need either globals or pass-through for codecs if they directly depend on the codecs needed. SkCodec use still relies on too many globals. SkResources currently uses `SkCodecs::get_decoders` as a global registry of codecs, but this is really just to keep Chromium limping along and Skia really should not have these globals (except maybe on a `SkLibrary` like thing). The SkCodecs side of this is that each SkResources instance should be maintaining its own list of codecs.

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message: Well, SkShaper and SkUnicode are also just interfaces, for which we implement a few common implementations that can be used, just like ResourceProvider. These aren't just selectors, any more than SkFontMgr is "just a selector".

subject: Add SkShapers::Factory as way to configure shaper behavior in svg/skottie
message:
`modules/skshaper/utils/FactoryHelpers.h` exists purely for convenience, anyone could implement an `SkShapers::Factory` with whatever the want.

SVG/Skottie can of course just select one of Skia's impls if they want, but that means that they need to depend on them directly. So yes, this is achievable at the build system level if SVG/Skottie  are willing to depend on one of Skia's impls directly.

Fix optimization setting for third_party libs in debug builds
message:
Ugh... thanks for pointing out something super simple but super complicated. This was added in https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/155760 because the idea was to always build third_party stuff with optimizations, since in theory we weren't developing these third_party projects so there was no reason to make our debug bot tests slower. In general the build is written around whatever the bots want, since in theory a developer can just tweak the build however they wish.

With this change there is actually no need at all for the predicate or setting the config at all, since it is set by default in a non-debug build [0] (`default_configs` is used below in `set_defaults`). The existing predicate simply exists to avoid adding the `optimize` config a second time.

Note that my local tweak to the build is usually to add `extra_cflags = ["-fno-omit-frame-pointer", "-g", "-O0" ]` to my `args.gn` to force everything to build in debug (the `extra_xxx` generally come after all the other flags, overriding them). This is why I haven't really looked into this, since I generally set up my `args.gn` once and then this doesn't bother me again for a while.

In any event, this isn't really as straight forward as it seems it should be. Will think about it.

[0] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/skia/gn/BUILDCONFIG.gn;l=184;drc=50012bd88eb956caf84f9465d65d8f544f1c0e26

subject: Reduce size of linear SkMaskGamma LUT
message: There is really no need for `std::vector` here to do what you want, let alone a `std::vector<std::vector>>`. If the idea was to push this allocation off to yet another heap allocation (`SkTMaskGamma` already always appears to be heap allocated) then this would be a `std::unique_ptr<uint8_t>` that the non-linear constructor assigns a heap region of the appropriate (constant) size.

subject: Reduce size of linear SkMaskGamma LUT
message: Yes, I just forgot to type the `[]`.

subject: Reduce size of linear SkMaskGamma LUT
message: With this change we no longer need `fIsLinear` either, since `fGammaTables` being nullptr already implies linear. Making this change makes `SkTMaskGamma` the size of a pointer (well, the size of a `std::unique_ptr<T[]>`, which is usually just a pointer) and also means `SkTMaskGamma()` can be constexpr. This means `gLinearMaskGamma` doesn't need to be `new`ed at all.

subject: [Fontations-backend] Color bitmap support.
message:
See `scaledemoji_rendering` gm with cbdt.ttf. The space glyph draws like the diamond. The space glyph is properly mapped to glyph 1, but there is no cblc/cbdt entry for glyph 1, which should cause the glyph to not be drawn. Instead of getting a "it's empty" signal this is instead returning the data for the next entry (which might be bad if it's after the last entry).

I think this is the "A small number of missing glyphs can be efficiently represented in formats 1 or 3 by having the offset for the missing glyph be followed by the same offset for the next glyph, thus indicating a data size of zero." case in [the specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/eblc#indexsubtable5-constant-metrics-glyphs-with-sparse-glyph-codes). Not sure how to handle this other than to find the location of the next glyph and see if it is equal? Not sure if this should be handled on this side or the skrifa / readfonts side. I'm somewhat surprised this doesn't happen for sbix since it works in a similar way, but it looks like that interface takes care of the glyph_data not being accessible / existing?

subject: Fix 'SkPath::conservativelyContainsRect' issue for closed cubic Bézier curves
message: Yeah, that looks equivalent to what's currently happening, though it's a little strange to put before the conic splitting since that returns false in this case for a different reason. There are only one split into two halves so there will be no "inside", but if there were three or more splits there could still be an inside.

subject: Fix 'SkPath::conservativelyContainsRect' issue for closed cubic Bézier curves
message:
I don't think we need or want this extra check? Then we could also remove the assert.

So the general idea here is that if the path is already known to be convex then a rect is contained inside the path if each verb of the path is outside and on the right "side" of the the rect (given the verb's slope), where quad and cubic verbs are approximated by the line between their start and end points. The issue being that if the start and end points are the same then that verb's edge line is zero length and doesn't have a direction and is "outside" all rects.

The argument is that completely degenerate verbs are ignored and quads get away with this because if the start and end points are at the same location then it is degenerate and currently any path which such a segment will not be considered convex. A conic will get chopped into two quads, so any convex conic should produce quads without the same start and end (but this will always return false for a circle?).

However, a cubic with the same start and end points can be convex. However, by the conservative rules here it should never contain any rects because the entire rectangle will always be on the "other side" of the verb's line edge away from the curve of the cubic. However, since this edge is degenerate it currently contains all rects instead of no rects.

As a result, it seems like testing for `SkPathVerb::kCubic` here isn't really needed? As the assert states, if we ever have `prevPt == pts[nextPt]` here we want to return false (since it means all rectangles are "outside" by the logic of this check). Since that's the case it could even be pushed down to `check_edge_against_rect` as a `if (p0 == p1) { return false; }`? Admittedly, this is probably extra work for the conic case and maybe the "segmentCount" use below, so I don't think we should do that, but it is logically what we want.

So while we can convince ourselves that at the moment only cubics need this check, it is generally true that in this conservative algorithm that if the first and last points a verb are the same then all rects are conservatively "outside" and we should immediately return false. So I don't think we need the extra check. We're going to fetch `pts[nextPt]` anyway, so it doesn't even avoid the load (which should be hot anyway, since it was just written).

message:

On the other hand, this is technically an `SkFreeDeleter` since the point is to use it as the `Deleter` template argument to `std::unique_ptr`. Though it does seem an odd name, since this is not for deleting `sk_free` but is a concrete instantiation of the `Deleter` concept / interface (though apparently it isn't spec'ed as a Concept yet). On my third hand this is `SkFreeFunctionObject` since the actual "C++ named requirement" this is implementing is `FunctionObject`.

Ugh, naming things.

subject: Add skia free wrapper for unique_ptr
message:
I don't mind the extra name, but I think I would much prefer this to be

`using SkFreeDeleter = SkOverloadedFunctionObject<void(void*), sk_free>;`

Though I realize this probably means splitting `SkOverloadedFunctionObject` and `SkFunctionObject` out of `SkTemplates.h` (or splitting everything else out of there) so that these can be included here. Then the `using` makes it obvious in the code that this is a convenience type, the `Overloaded` part makes it obvious in the code that we're doing this because we believe the function may be overloaded, and then the comment only needs to be "OpenSSL declares a function which may be named sk_free."

subject: Add skia free wrapper for unique_ptr
message:
In fact, I would much prefer that `SkFunctionWrapper` be left alone in general (so that it can be used both for `sk_free` and other things in the future that may require disambiguation) and prefer to introduce something here like

`template <auto p> using SkFunctionObject = SkFunctionWrapper<std::remove_pointer_t<decltype(p)>, p>;`

and then use `SkFunctionObject` where it can be used (when the function is not overloaded). In fact, at the same time `SkFunctionWrapper` could be renamed to `SkOverloadedFunctionWrapper`, since that's essentially the only time it would be used.

subject: Remove Sk4pxXfermode
message:
After much poking about with perf and looking through the history of this, raster pipeline has already been used to replace what it is faster at. The remaining bits of Sk4xXfermode blending left are the bits that are faster. The raster pipeline is fast and very consistently so. However, it appears that the issue may be how much inlining can be done. Some of the Sk4x routines, like clear and plus, can be inlined and optimized to death. The other interesting part is that raster pipeline must check for edges (spin-up, spin-down) inside the load and store routines and these checks cannot be lifted out of the loop.

There doesn't appear to be any real logical difference between what raster pipeline and the Sk4x opts are doing here. The Sk4x opts are essentially what one would get if dumping the rater pipeline stages for each xfer mode for a specific architecture and then letting the compiler have a go at each one, effectively just doing lots of inlining.

Essentially, raster pipeline assembles pipelines at runtime by assembling function pointers; Sk4x assembles pipleines at compile time by assembling code through template specialization. The actual awkwardness (and the reason to propose removing these opts at all) is that they aren't actually the same. It would be really nice to have a way to generically have raster pipeline produce compile time optimizable code and then allow the user to select for which architectures opts should be generated. The one thing which would be required to change in raster pipeline would be to make "uniforms" (like the src, dst, alpha) parameterizable somehow (currently those pointers are baked into the raster pipeline).

Typical perf results:
Old           New
0.11 ±  5%    0.27 ±  4%  155%  blendmicro_sprite_SrcOut
0.10 ±  8%    0.27 ±  4%  161%  blendmicro_sprite_SrcIn
0.10 ±  0%    0.27 ±  3%  163%  blendmicro_sprite_DstIn
0.10 ±  6%    0.27 ±  6%  163%  blendmicro_sprite_DstOut
0.10 ±  1%    0.29 ±  4%  179%  blendmicro_sprite_DstOver
0.09 ±  3%    0.27 ±  6%  204%  blendmicro_sprite_Modulate
0.09 ±  8%    0.30 ±  3%  212%  blendmicro_sprite_Screen
0.05 ±  4%    0.25 ±  5%  441%  blendmicro_sprite_Clear
0.04 ±  2%    0.26 ±  4%  528%  blendmicro_sprite_Plus

subject: Remove Sk4pxXfermode
message:
Alas, in the case of Plus (since it was the biggest unexpected outlier I took a look into it) the Sk4x version does `s.saturatedAdd(d)` which turns directly into a single _mm_adds_epu8 (paddusb) instruction, while raster pipeline's plus is `min(s+d, 255)` which turns into many more instructions. However, the actual plus implementation isn't the hotspot in the raster pipeline.

The Sk4x version knows that it is written against SkPMColor and so is just load some SkPMColors, so this nice instruction (SkXfermode only works on SkPMColor), and the directly store it. On the other hand raster pipeline is more generic. Even though we do get the lowp raster pipeline the part taking the most time is the loads and stores and packing and unpacking the r, g, b, a lanes (and working in U16 instead of directly with the U8 data).

The overhead of getting the data in and out of the raster pipeline isn't usually all that bad, since the original idea was to build up a substantial pipeline. However, the overhead is high compared to doing a single actual manipulation stage in the pipeline (just the xfermode).

After digging through some perf stall events, I don't know that the difference is really memory access patterns or stalls. Both the opts and raster pipeline keep above 2 instructions per clock on my machine, so even though there are memory stalls recorded the CPU does keep moving.
